newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislator unveils alternative bridge plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislator unveils alternative bridge plan.

text.p: A California state assemblyman introduced legislation on Monday to fund bridge improvements in the state without requiring toll increases.

Republican Assemblyman Gary Miller said his measure would raise more than $2 billion to retrofit seven state toll bridges, five of which are located in the San Francisco Bay area. The other two are in southern California.
In contrast with proposals by San Francisco Bay area lawmakers, Miller said his legislation would not "penalize the rest of the state" to fund Bay area bridge improvements.
Miller's legislation would allocate $650 million in existing bond funds, $300 million in state gas taxes and $1.1 billion of existing toll bridge revenues to the projects.

The bill would not require toll increases on any of the bridges. The assemblyman said enough money was being generated from existing tolls in the San Francisco Bay area to support bonds to fund the needed improvements.

If local government authorities want additional revenues, Miller said his measure would allow them to raise tolls. But he said these tolls would be available exclusively to pay for the needed retrofit work.
Some San Francisco Bay area lawmakers favor a plan that would require more than $1.6 billion in state funds to be used along with $440 million in locally generated toll revenues.
"Their plan would be a massive subsidy of the Bay area by the Central Valley and southern California," Miller said.
Miller's bill is expected to be heard for the first time in late March in the Assembly Transportation Committee.
